subject.title: PR3/5 durable core: wake targets, producers, and replay

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this core durable-runtime ledger and five-PR release stack as the canonical owner of restart-safe agent, subagent, wake, and replay state?
rationale: The PR adds a broad persisted runtime model, new Gateway and environment surfaces, and parallel lifecycle state; code review cannot choose whether that architecture should replace or coexist with current task, subagent, session, and delivery owners.

options.title: Canonicalize, then sponsor
options.body: Require the durable store to become the authoritative lifecycle path, remove best-effort mirroring, prove upgrades and live replay, then land in stack order.

options.title: Sponsor mirror semantics
options.body: Explicitly accept a non-authoritative observational ledger and document that failed mirror writes may omit wake and replay records.

options.title: Pause the core stack
options.body: Retain existing task, subagent, session, and durable-delivery owners and use current extension surfaces for optional orchestration.

recommendation.title: Canonicalize, then sponsor
recommendation.body: Require the durable store to become the authoritative lifecycle path, remove best-effort mirroring, prove upgrades and live replay, then land in stack order.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans core Gateway architecture, public runtime surface, release sequencing, and persisted-state ownership.
